Here is a Python script to generate a palindrome of length 255:

```python
import random

def generate_palindrome(length):
    half_length = length // 2
    palindrome = ''.join([chr(random.randint(33, 126)) for _ in range(half_length)])
    return palindrome + palindrome[::-1] if length % 2 == 0 else palindrome + palindrome[:-1][::-1]

print(generate_palindrome(255))
```

This script generates a random string of characters between ASCII values 33 and 126 (which is almost the whole printable range) and then concatenates it with its reverse. The resulting string will be a palindrome.

Please note that due to the randomness of character generation, you might get different palindromes each time you run this script.
